Excellent! So after Qxg6+ both Kh8 and Kf8 lose to Qg8#. The only defense is Nxg6. After Qxg6+ Nxg6, White continues with Rexg6+ (as analyzed) and wins decisively. This is the key move!

**Best move:** Qxg6+

**Main line:** Qxg6+ Kh8 (or Kf8) Qg8#, or if Nxg6 then Rexg6+ winning material.

**Motif:** fork (the queen checks the king and attacks the pinned pawn and rook)

**Explanation (coaching note):**
When a piece is pinned to the king, it's trapped and vulnerable. Here, g6 is pinned by your rook to the enemy king. Capture it with check (Qxg6+)—this is a fork hitting the king and the g6 pawn. If the king moves to h8 or f8, you have an immediate back-rank mate with Qg8#. If Black captures with Nxg6, you recapture with Rexg6+, winning more material. Always look for forcing moves when your opponent has a pinned piece.
